h: Sacred Times Reveal Providence Beyond What We Can Expect

p: "The appointed times of Hashem, which you shall proclaim
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י (פָּרָשַׁת בֹּא, שְׁמוֹת יב, טז)
"'A calling of holiness' is a noun:
That is: through the Beis Din
the appointed times are fixed automatically.
And so too in the holy Zohar on this parashah
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִלְּשׁוֹן קְרִיאָה וְהַזְמָנָה
This too is from the language of calling and invitation.
that it is from the language of
for there too it is the language of happening,
"If a bird's nest happens before you,"
So it is the language of an occurrence:
whatever day on which it occurs,
And this fits a Yom Tov,
which is fixed according to the sanctification of the month
and is not fixed to its day.
But Shabbos, which is fixed and established
why is it included among the callings of holiness?
Now "mikreh" is always with a heh,
and here it is written with an aleph.
And in Koheles we find it written (Koheles 2:14),
מִקְרֶה אֶחָד יִקְרֶה אֶת כּוּלָּם וְגוֹ׳
וּמִקְרֶה אֶחָד לָהֶם וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם ג, יט)
"One happening to the tzaddik and to the rasha, etc.";
כִּי עֵת וָפֶגַע יִקְרֶה אֶת כּוּלָּם וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם, יא)
"For time and chance befall them all, etc." (Koheles 9:11).
אֵיךְ תָּלָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הַכֹּל בְּמִקְרֶה
how could he, chas v'shalom, attribute everything to happenstance?
Even with a beast and with animals,
it is not by happenstance, chas v'shalom,
as they said in the Yerushalmi
כַּד שְׁמַע בַּת קוֹל מִן שְׁמַיָּא
when he heard a heavenly voice from Heaven
and how much more so with a person!
But in truth we find in the Torah too
that the Holy One, blessed is He, said
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
הֲיִקְרְךָ דְבָרִי אִם לֹא (בְּמִדְבַּר יא, כג)
"Will My word befall you or not?" (Bamidbar 11:23);
and likewise we find that Eliezer said,
הַקְרֵה נָא לְפָנַי הַיּוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית כד, יב)
וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר
and likewise Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, said,
כִּי הִקְרָה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְפָנָי (שָׁם כז, כ)
"For Hashem your God made it happen before me" (Bereishis 27:20).
that which a person does not expect to come,
That is: all the events of the world
"Learn from this that the hour stands for me";
And regarding the wicked we find (Berachos 7b):
"A rasha for whom the hour smiles."
That is: the last attribute is called "time,"
as is written in the holy Zohar
the attributes for the creation of the world;
and this attribute is called "the hour,"
and this is mikreh with a heh,
for it is the last heh,
And this is what it says:
כִּי עֵת וָפֶגַע יִקְרֶה אֶת כּוּלָּם
"For time and chance befall them all,"
for in truth everything is from Hashem Yisbarach.
וְכֵן בֶּאֱלִיעֶזֶר שֶׁאָמַר הַקְרֵה נָא לְפָנַי
And so with Eliezer, who said, "Make it happen before me":
although it would come by providence from Hashem Yisbarach,
nevertheless the maiden, for her part,
and would go in her innocence,
so the language of happening applies.
And so with Rus, of whom it is written (Rus 2:3),
the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, etc.":
שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמָשִׁיחַ
the line of David HaMelech, peace be upon him, and Mashiach,
it was by way of happenstance,
but it was by providence from Hashem Yisbarach.
and in it there are twenty-eight times,
for good and for the opposite.
And so in the matter of the meat:
but only that they be satisfied with the mann;
אָמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָתֵת לָהֶם בָּשָׂר
did Hashem Yisbarach say to give them meat;
and therefore He called the matter,
even from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
and said, "Will My word befall you?"

p: in the command of Hashem Yisbarach to Moshe
לֵךְ וְאָסַפְתָּ אֶת זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
"Go and gather the elders of Yisrael, etc.,
and you and the elders of Yisrael shall come, etc.:
Hashem, the God of the Hebrews, happened upon us"
and afterward, when Moshe and Aharon came,
"The God of the Hebrews called upon us"
then the matter would have come
which would have been in completeness
it is written as happening with a heh.
when the elders slipped away one by one,
even though they were not worthy of redemption.
And so with the splitting of the Yam Suf,
when there was an accusation against them,
as is written in the holy Zohar
that the splitting of the Yam Suf
And so with what Yaakov said,
he sought to reveal the end to them.
That is: Ben David does not come
until they despair of the redemption,
That is, the end "in its time";
for the end of "I will hasten it"
but "Today, if you will listen to His voice"
Rather, he sought to reveal to them
And this is what they said (in Tanchuma Vayechi 8):
"He sought to reveal the end to them.
A parable: to what is the matter comparable?
and their deed of sale, etc."
This is the end "in its time,"
which is their deed of sale:
that even if, chas v'shalom, they will be
a generation that is entirely guilty,
Hashem will act for His own sake,
as it was at the Exodus from Egypt.
Therefore it is written "that which will befall,"
which will not arise in the heart.
And it is written with an aleph,
which is the supernal hidden one,
And so regarding Amalek it is written (Devarim 25:18),
"Who happened upon you on the way":
it was by way of happenstance,
after all the nations had seen and heard of
the Exodus from Egypt and the splitting of the Yam Suf,
so who would come against them?
Yet he strode four hundred parsaos
(as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 9).
And such is the power of this kelipah:
in a place he would never imagine.
And it uses the language "happened upon you,"
like "Will My word befall you, etc.";
for all the exiles came about
to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
"And afterward they will go out with great wealth":
it was from Hashem Yisbarach, for this purpose.
And so with the exile of Ashur:
although the Ten Tribes were assimilated among them,
they are messengers from Hashem Yisbarach.
Not so the kelipah of Amalek,
which is the kelipah of the dog,
which is the inner part of "ox" and "donkey,"
as is written in the holy Zohar
are the kelipah of Esav and Yishmael;
and the inner part of שור, which is ו,
and of חמור, which is מו,
and when there is an accuser,
אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וָדִין
then Hashem Yisbarach executes justice and judgment,
even though there was no will to punish them.
And this is the expression "who happened upon you."
And so it is expounded regarding Haman
בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל קָרְהוּ בָּא עֲלֵיכֶם
the grandson of 'who happened upon you' has come upon you."
For this too was a thing
but who ever heard of such a thing
to bring out an entire nation to slaughter
And even Achashverosh, who had it in his heart,
as they said in the Gemara (Megillah 14a)
in the parable of the owner of the mound and the owner of the ditch,
and this is "the first of nations, Amalek,"
which is beyond the grasp of the intellect.
And he accused above as well
"And the laws of the king they do not keep";
"Wherever it says in the Megillah, etc.,
it implies the holy and the profane";
that is, "the laws of the King,"
of the King of kings as well.
And as for what he said,
"I will weigh out into the king's treasuries,"
we said that his intent was
to weigh out so large a sum for charity;
for this is the kelipah of Amalek,
that Yisrael are not so good.
And about this they said in the Gemara (Megillah 13b):
"He preceded their shekalim to his shekalim."
בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל קָרְךָ בָּא עֲלֵיכֶם
"The grandson of 'who happened upon you' has come upon you,"
And so is the matter of the holiness of the festivals:
from the six days of Creation
Pesach, of which it is written (Shemos 12:42),
and already from the days of Avraham the night was prepared,
as they said in the Midrash
and likewise the seventh day of Pesach was prepared
for the splitting of the Yam Suf,
"One who is destined to sing shirah
at the sea on this day, etc.";
and likewise the sixth of Sivan:
"one who is destined to receive the Torah
from Mount Sinai on this day, etc.";
and likewise it is written in the account of Creation,
which alludes to the sixth of Sivan
the holiness of the festivals depends on Yisrael,
through the fixing of the new months.
that they can instill holiness into time
by way of happening and chance;
regarding a month that was seen, etc."
And whatever day happens to them
they will instill holiness into it;
and therefore they are called "happenings of holiness."
are a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,
and there was no understanding at all

p: מְקַפֵּץ עַל הַגְּבָעוֹת (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ח)
which is the supernal hidden one;
and therefore "mikra" is stated with an aleph.
the mitzvah came as a remembrance of the act of Creation:
just as I rested on it"
that Yisrael should instill holiness into Shabbos,
and through this they would merit
the holiness of the Shabbos of Hashem Yisbarach.
"And with what do you sanctify it?
With food, drink and clean clothing,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה נָשֹׂא י, א
and so wrote the Baal HaTurim:
And this too is a happening
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת עֵקֶב)
as they said (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Eikev, Devarim Rabbah 3:1):
גַּם כֵּן שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף
so too, through the pleasure of the body
a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,
which came about as a happening beyond the intellect.
That is why there is mentioned
the remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,

Halakha: If …”
